# RustyNES v2.4.7 "Keystone"

**The stack closes, and a dead line proves itself dead.**

A keystone is the wedge at the top of an arch that holds every other stone in place; the stack group is the 6502's, because subroutines, interrupts and the return path all rest on it. With this release the 6502's stack group, `JSR`/`RTS`/`RTI`, and `JMP` in both its forms are implemented in SystemVerilog in the sibling repository, and rung 1 stands at **four ROMs, 752 records, matching the oracle on all seven CPU fields**, with seven mutations demonstrated to break the gate. `opgroup4` contributes 179 records and every construct in it is new to this release; the three earlier ROMs are re-run unchanged at 147, 140 and 286.

Written from public documentation only — the NESdev wiki's 6502 cycle-time, instruction and addressing-mode pages, and this project's own `docs/cpu-6502.md`. No reference NES core was opened; none is present in the tree.

## The oracle found a real RTL bug before any mutation did

`JMP ($C090)` reached `$77A0` instead of `$C0A0`. Cycle 3 latched the fetched vector low byte into `adl`, **destroying the pointer low byte**, so cycle 4 computed `{adh, vector_low + 1}` rather than `{adh, pointer_low + 1}` — and `$77` is simply what sits one past the vector. A third latch (`vec_lo`) fixes it.

That is the rung working exactly as designed rather than a lucky catch: the divergence named the instruction, and the wrong value said which byte had been read. This is the first defect in the programme that co-simulation found on its own, ahead of the mutation pass built to look for defects.

## `JMP ($xxFF)` does not cross the page

Hardware fetches the low byte from `$C1FF` and the high byte from `$C100` — not `$C200`. The test ROM places a vector at `$C1FF` on purpose and places a **distinct** sentinel at `$C200`, so an implementation that "corrects" the bug with a 16-bit increment jumps somewhere visibly different rather than somewhere plausible. A test that lands on a plausible address is a test that agrees with the wrong answer.

## Verilator caught an enum overflow that would have aliased two opcodes

`op_e` was `logic [4:0]` — 32 values — and this release took it to 33. The rejection is the good outcome: a silently-wrapped enum decodes one opcode as another with no diagnostic anywhere, and the resulting divergence would have pointed at whichever instruction happened to alias rather than at the declaration. Widened to six bits.

## Two mutations came back NOT CAUGHT, for different reasons

**`PHP` pushing the raw `P` was invisible**, because a `PHP`/`PLP` round-trip *cannot* see bits 4 and 5: `PHP` sets them, `PLP` masks them off, and the two errors cancel exactly. The ROM now does `PHP` then `PLA`, pulling the pushed byte into a register where it is compared unmasked — and the two answers differ by `$30`.

**`JSR` pushing the wrong address was invisible** for a different and more interesting reason: the mutation targeted `store_val`, which the `AM_JSR` bus block never reads — it drives `dout` directly. The arm was **dead code**, and the mutation not failing is what said so. Removed; re-run against the real site, it diverges.

A mutation that cannot fail is evidence about the code it mutated, not about the test. That is a different lesson from the previous two releases, where the ROM was at fault; here one was the ROM and one was the RTL carrying a line nothing could reach.

## Also modelled

A push is three cycles and a pull is four; the pull's extra cycle is a dummy read at the stack pointer **before** it increments. `JSR` is six, with its own dummy stack read. `RTS` increments the pulled PC and `RTI` does not — because `JSR` pushes the address of its last byte while an interrupt pushes the address to resume at.

## Two gates that could not gate what they claimed

**`cpu-gate` hardcoded `--cycles 301` for every ROM.** `cpu-smoke` already varied the window; the target the documentation calls *the* accuracy gate did not, so running it on `opgroup3` compared only the first 136 of its 286 records. It **failed closed** — `cpu_boot_trace_diff` exits non-zero on a length mismatch, which is the only reason this was a usability defect rather than the failure this project keeps finding — but a gate that cannot be invoked correctly is a gate nobody invokes, and the two ROMs it could not gate were the two most recent. Each window now lives in one variable both targets read, and an unknown ROM is refused rather than silently given a default.

**The oracle/DUT window pairing is off by one, and now documented.** The oracle's `--boot-trace 0..N` yields N records where the harness's `--cycles N` yields N−1, so `opgroup3` pairs `0..600` against `--cycles 601`. Feed it `0..601` instead and the diff reports `reference=287 actual=286` — a one-record length mismatch indistinguishable, at a glance, from the CPU halting a cycle early. That is a debugging trap aimed squarely at the RTL for a defect that lives in the invocation.

## The record counts are measured now, and measuring is what found those two

`docs/mister.md` claimed 573 records above a table whose rows summed to 455. Both figures were true; they were counted under different capture windows. `opgroup1` closed v2.4.4 over a 0..64 cycle window and was reported then as 29 records, and v2.4.5 widened every window to reach the addressing modes, so the same ROM now yields 147.

The correction was first derived by *subtracting* two published totals — 573 − 140 − 286 — which gave the right answer and could not have found either defect above. Re-derived by running `cpu-gate` against a freshly exported golden for each ROM, all four counts are now **measured**: 147, 140, 286, 179. A number reached by arithmetic over two unverified numbers is the documentation-side form of a check reporting a pass it has not earned.

## A fourth place release-state drift moved to

`to-dos/ROADMAP.md` called v2.3.9 "the current tag", six releases stale. That is the **fourth** location this drift has occupied, and each move followed the previous one being gated: the 15 release anchors, then the `(current)` labels, then the unshipped-status labels, and now a narrative sentence naming a tag in *different words*. So `release_state_prose_audit` gained a third rule rather than the sentence gaining a correction — and it fired on this very release cut, catching `to-dos/ROADMAP.md:62 calls v2.4.6 the current tag, but the workspace is at 2.4.7` before the notes were written. <!-- release-state: not-a-claim -->

The phrase list is deliberately two entries. "current release" appears 14 times in the corpus and "the latest release" 3, almost all generic prose with no version attached; a rule over those would report findings nobody can act on, which is how a check gets switched off.

## Verification

No crate under `rustynes-{cpu,ppu,apu,mappers,core}` changes, so **AccuracyCoin 141/141 (100.00%, RAM decoder) and nestest 0-diff hold by construction** rather than needing re-verification.
